sec: Thyroid Storm Protocol & Acute, Subacute, Chronic Thyroiditis

items.q: Match the clinical features of thyrotoxic crisis (thyroid storm) — 1) Predisposing factors 2) Presenting features … A) Inadequate treatment before radiotherapy, surgery, acute illness B) Arrhythmia, fever with delirium, seizures
items.exp: Predisposing factors: inadequate treatment before radiotherapy, surgery, illness; Presenting features: arrhythmia, fever with delirium, seizure. (Book p914)

items.q: What is the specific dosing regimen of Propylthiouracil (PTU) in the management of thyrotoxic crisis on page 914?
opts: 1000 mg stat loading dose, followed by 250 mg Q4H
100 mg stat, followed by 50 mg TDS
2000 mg as a single daily dose
items.exp: Under thyrotoxic crisis management: 'Propylthiouracil : 1000mg stat -> 250mg Q4H'. (Book p914)

items.q: In thyrotoxic crisis management, oral iodine is administered as ___ (500 mg BD) to exploit the ___ effect.
items.exp: Under management: 'Oral iodine : Iopanoic acid 500mg BD (Wolff-Chaikoff effect)'. (Book p914)

items.q: What is the propranolol dose specified for thyrotoxic crisis on page 914?
items.exp: For thyrotoxic crisis, propranolol is dosed at '60mg Q4H' (compared to 40 mg Q6H in routine thyrotoxicosis). (Book p914)

items.q: Match the etiology of acute thyroiditis to its clinical features — 1) Post-infection 2) Non-infectious acute causes … A) Children, follows staph/strep, pyriform sinus site, normal TFT, pain B) Radiation induced, trauma induced
items.exp: Acute thyroiditis branches into: Post-infection (children, follows staph/strep, site: piriform sinus, TFT normal, pain), Radiation induced, and Trauma induced. (Book p914)

items.q: An 8-year-old child presents with sudden severe anterior neck tenderness and fever following streptococcal pharyngitis. TFTs are completely normal. Scintigraphy reveals an infected tract originating from the piriform sinus. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Acute post-infection thyroiditis occurs in children, follows staph/strep, arises from a piriform sinus fistula, presents with pain, and has normal TFTs. (Book p914)

items.q: Assess acute thyroiditis: I Thyroid function tests (TFT) are characteristically normal. II Local pain is the primary presenting symptom.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: For Acute Thyroiditis: 'TFT : Normal' and 'Symptom : Pain'. (Book p914)

items.q: Match the synonymous names for Subacute Thyroiditis — 1) Eponymous designation 2) Pathological designation 3) Viral relationship … A) De Quervain's thyroiditis B) Granulomatous thyroiditis C) Post-viral (with no direct viral association established)
items.exp: Under Subacute Thyroiditis: 'De Quervain's/Subacute thyroiditis : AKA Granulomatous/viral thyroiditis. Post-viral (no viral association)'. (Book p914)

items.q: Which HLA allele is strongly associated with subacute (de Quervain's) thyroiditis on page 914?
items.exp: Under Subacute Thyroiditis Features: 'HLA : B-35'. (Book p914)

items.q: On radionuclide scintigraphy, subacute (de Quervain's) thyroiditis characteristically shows ___ uptake.
items.exp: Features of subacute thyroiditis: 'No uptake in Scintigraphy', also depicted in the scan image 'Subacute thyroiditis : No uptake in scintigraphy'. (Book p914)

items.q: A 52-year-old man presents with a stony hard, painless neck mass with dense fibrous tissue infiltrating adjacent soft tissues. Serology reveals elevated IgG4 levels. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Chronic Thyroiditis includes Riedel's thyroiditis: 'AKA IgG4-related disease, Painless hard thyroid, Dense fibrosis'. (Book p914)

items.q: Assess Riedel's thyroiditis on page 914: I It is recognized as an IgG4-related disease. II The physical hallmark is a painless, hard thyroid with dense fibrosis.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Riedel's thyroiditis: AKA IgG4-related disease, Painless hard thyroid, Dense fibrosis. (Book p914)
